Revised assessment: The FOMC’s “hawkish hold”—keeping the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continuing balance-sheet runoff—aligns with Taylor-rule/New Keynesian guidance when inflation is still above target (Clarida–Galí–Gertler) and acknowledges long, uncertain transmission lags (Romer & Romer; Bernanke–Mihov). QT and higher money-market rates tighten financial conditions and likely lift term premia via the yield-curve channel (Cochrane–Piazzesi), supporting the statement that credit conditions will weigh on activity. However, easing inflation, a resilient banking system, and credible, independent policy with forward guidance help anchor expectations (consistent with Bernanke’s emphasis on independence and Bagehot-style backstops), moderating downside risks. Net tone: slightly negative, but less so than before.
